subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or per-agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current code, tests, and docs treat `/exec` as persistent session state, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because older session state can shadow later operator policy changes.

options.title: Clamp session exec to operator policy
options.body: Treat global or per-agent exec policy as the upper bound and clear or clamp stored session fields that would exceed it, with focused migration/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep session overrides authoritative
options.body: Preserve current behavior and document that operators must use tool policy, `sessions.patch`, or an explicit reset flow to enforce changed policy for existing sessions.

options.title: Add explicit reset or doctor first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing persisted sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp session exec to operator policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or per-agent exec policy as the upper bound and clear or clamp stored session fields that would exceed it, with focused migration/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest feature-history trail for `/exec` session overrides and current precedence coverage points to this owner path.
